review_notes: I read the whole file, the definition of IsLocallyNormalRing and of_ringEquiv in Normal.lean, and Mathlib's Localization.AtPrime.mapPiEvalRingHom and its bijectivity lemma. The same ofBijective equivalence and the same transport pattern appear four times, across the two bullets of `pi` and the two bullets of `of_pi`. The `pi_iff` theorem only assembles the other two, so it is fine. I did not compile any of the proposed rewrites. The helper's exact instance and unification behaviour, such as the `comap` form of the prime, is untested.

findings.declaration: IsLocallyNormalRing.pi and IsLocallyNormalRing.of_pi (four copies of the localization equivalence and transport)
findings.problem: The four bullets of `pi` and `of_pi` each rebuild the same ring equivalence `Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom S i)) ≃+* Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal` from `mapPiEvalRingHom` and its bijectivity. Each bullet then repeats the same transport argument: introduce the hypothesis as a local `let _` instance, then push `IsDomain` or `IsIntegrallyClosed` across the equivalence. The `pi` proof also repeats the `obtain`/`subst` step, and the `of_pi` proof repeats the `⟨q.asIdeal.comap _, inferInstance⟩` prime construction. The only differences are the direction of the equivalence and which of the two properties is transported. Any change to the equivalence has to be made in four places.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma stating that for `q : PrimeSpectrum (S i)`, the conjunction `IsDomain A ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed A` holds for `A = Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom S i))` exactly when it holds for `Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal`. Alternatively, define the equivalence once as a private `def piEvalLocalizationEquiv (q : PrimeSpectrum (S i)) : Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom S i)) ≃+* Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal := RingEquiv.ofBijective _ (Localization.AtPrime.mapPiEvalRingHom_bijective _)`. Prove the lemma with `IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv` and `MulEquiv.isDomain` applied to this equivalence and its symm. Then `pi` obtains `i, q` from `PrimeSpectrum.exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq`, substitutes, and uses the `←` direction with the instances at `q` from the hypotheses. `of_pi` instantiates the `→` direction at the prime `⟨q.asIdeal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom S i), inferInstance⟩` supplied by `IsLocallyNormalRing (∀ i, S i)`. Each theorem then becomes about five lines, and the equivalence is built once. The hypotheses are unchanged: `pi` keeps `[Finite I]` for the `exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq` step, and `of_pi` stays universe-polymorphic with no finiteness assumption.
findings.benefit: The roughly 45 lines of near-identical boilerplate shrink to one equivalence and one iff lemma. The two main theorems then read as the mathematical statement: local normality at q transfers to the localization at the pulled-back prime, in either direction. The `pi` and `of_pi` proofs can no longer drift apart.
